title: Do Charge Prediction Models Learn Legal Theory?

bias_targets.methodology: Applying probing tasks on sentence representations and perturbation experiments (substituting common textual circumstances with uncommon ones, like 'armed with a knife' vs. 'armed with a baton') to determine if models rely on spurious textual correlations rather than actual legal knowledge.

Evaluating model predictions on incomplete fact descriptions (where sentences related to required criminal elements are removed) to test whether models fail to follow the presumption of innocence and incorrectly continue to predict guilty charges.
